summary: Inspect the supplied evidence and distinguish what each check establishes.

steps.title: Publish and consume exact image content

blocks.text: Keep the publication reference distinct from the exact-content retrieval reference.
ECR repositories store container images; assigned image digests identify the content.
Authenticate Docker by piping aws ecr get-login-password --region REGION to docker login --username AWS --password-stdin REGISTRY.
Tag the already-built image as REGISTRY/REPOSITORY:TAG, then docker push that reference.
Retrieve exact content with docker pull REGISTRY/REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST. Verify access separately with the approved publisher and consumer identities.

steps.title: Work through the evidence: Publish and consume exact image content

blocks.text: Use the supplied Region and registry for authentication, then tag and push the already-built image with the approved publisher. Record its digest. The approved consumer pulls that exact digest and checks its own access. Publisher success does not establish consumer access; retain both identity-specific outcomes.
A convenient tag is not the stated exact-content retrieval test. Publishing alone is not verified consumption.

items.text:
Approved publisher: aws ecr get-login-password --region REGION | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin REGISTRY; tag already-built image REGISTRY/REPOSITORY:TAG; docker push REGISTRY/REPOSITORY:TAG succeeds. Publication digest recorded as DIGEST.
Separately prepared approved consumer: same Docker authentication for supplied registry/Region; docker pull REGISTRY/REPOSITORY@sha256:DIGEST succeeds. Retrieved digest equals publication digest; both identity-specific outcomes retained.

Approved publisher authenticates, tags and successfully pushes; publication digest recorded. Separately authenticated approved consumer successfully pulls REGISTRY/REPOSITORY:TAG; retrieved digest is not compared.
Conclusion: exact published digest retrieval verified.

Publisher authenticates, tags and pushes, and pulls its own publication by recorded digest. No separately prepared consumer authentication or pull recorded.
Conclusion: publisher and consumer access both verified.

i1.message: Authentication, tagged push, recorded digest and separately authenticated consumer retrieval by that digest are all present.

i2.message: Tag retrieval without matching the recorded digest does not establish retrieval of the exact published image.

i3.message: The publisher’s self-retrieval omits the separately prepared approved consumer access evidence.

correct.message: Each judgement follows the supplied excerpt and the verification criterion.

incorrect.message: Check the evidence behind each conclusion; a partial success does not establish every required boundary.

hints: Track publication and retrieval separately, including the consumer’s reference.

steps.title: The verification sequence: Trace an immutable build artifact

blocks.text: For the supplied output file, set id-token: write, contents: read and attestations: write. Use actions/attest@v4 with subject-path set to that file, then actions/upload-artifact@v4 with path set to it and the supplied revision-based name. Retain the run, artifact name and upload SHA256 digest as the immutable content reference; v4 artifacts are immutable.

Use actions/download-artifact: it checks the upload SHA256 digest and warns on mismatch. Verify the extracted output’s provenance with gh attestation verify PATH/TO/YOUR/BUILD/ARTIFACT-BINARY -R ORGANIZATION_NAME/REPOSITORY_NAME --format json. Before deployment, inspect the verified attestation’s source revision and build workflow/run.

steps.title: Work through the evidence: Trace an immutable build artifact

blocks.text: For the supplied orders output at rev-42, attest and upload the same file using the required permissions and revision-based name. Retain the run, name and upload digest. After download, inspect any mismatch warning and verify the extracted file’s attestation for the approved repository, revision and workflow/run.
Download integrity and provenance are different checks. A digest-mismatch warning is not a promise to block every mismatch, nor proof of the intended source revision.

steps.title: Check trace an immutable build artifact
steps.lede: Read the supplied evidence in this step and choose the interpretation it supports.

public.prompt: actions/download-artifact reports no upload SHA256 mismatch. Which additional evidence verifies provenance before deployment?

options.text: Inspect only the revision-based artifact name.
Run gh attestation verify on the extracted file for the intended repository and inspect its verified source revision and build workflow/run.
Treat the download digest check alone as verified source revision and build provenance.

o1.message: The name is not a substitute for verifying the file’s attestation and inspecting its source and build linkage.

o2.message: This follows the stated evidence and the taught verification rule.

o3.message: The download check verifies upload integrity, not the verified attestation’s source and build linkage.

public.prompt: Read each workflow/publication excerpt and decide whether it attests and immutably publishes the same supplied orders release for rev-42, retains its publication record, and verifies its source/build linkage after download. The supplied revision-based name is rev-42.

items.text:
permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read
  attestations: write
steps:
  - uses: actions/attest@v4
    with:
      subject-path: releases/orders.zip
  - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
    with:
      path: releases/orders.zip
      name: rev-42
Record: completed workflow attested and uploaded that file; workflow run, rev-42 artifact name and upload SHA256 digest retained together.
Download record: actions/download-artifact reports no upload SHA256 mismatch. gh attestation verify on the extracted releases/orders.zip for the approved repository succeeds. The verified attestation binds that file’s digest to the approved source repository, revision rev-42 and the build workflow/run matching the retained publication record.

permissions: id-token: write; contents: read; attestations: write. actions/attest@v4 subject-path: releases/orders.zip. actions/upload-artifact@v4 path: a different supplied output; name: rev-42. Completed run retained with upload SHA256.
Conclusion: provenance and publication describe the same file.

permissions: id-token: write; contents: read; attestations: write. actions/attest@v4 and actions/upload-artifact@v4 both target releases/orders.zip, upload name rev-42. Run completes. Publication record retains only rev-42, omitting workflow run and upload SHA256.
Conclusion: immutable content reference and build-run linkage retained.

i1.message: The same file is attested and uploaded, the immutable publication record is retained, and extracted-file verification establishes the matching source revision and build workflow/run.

i2.message: The attestation subject and uploaded file differ; retained metadata does not fix that mismatch.

i3.message: The required publication record needs the workflow run and upload SHA256 digest as well as the name.

correct.message: Each judgement follows the supplied excerpt and the verification criterion.

incorrect.message: Check the evidence behind each conclusion; a partial success does not establish every required boundary.

hints: Compare the two file paths and look for all three retained publication references.
